questions.question:
Select the option that is related to the fourth term in the same way as the first term is related to the second term and the fifth term is related to the sixth term.

169 : 14 :: ? : 16 :: 289 : 18
questions.solution:
**Logic :** Square of (2nd number - 1) = 1st number

So,

 
• 169 : 14

(14 - 1)² = 169

(13)² = 169

169 = 169 (LHS = RHS)

And,

 
• 289 : 18</

questions.question:
Study the given pattern carefully and select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in it.

(6, 1, 18)

(5, 4, 60)

(6, 2, ?)

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)
questions.solution:
Logic : (1st number × 2nd number) = (3rd number ÷ 3)

So,

 
• (6, 1, 18)

6 × 1 = 18 ÷ 3

6 = 6 (LHS = RHS)

And,

 
• (5, 4, 60)

5 × 4 = 60 ÷ 3

20 = 20 (LHS = RHS)

Similarly,

 
• (6, 2, ?)

6 × 2 = ? ÷ 3

12 × 3 = ?

36 = ?

Hence, "36" is the correct answer.

Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

Some teachers are scientists.

All scientists are doctors.

All doctors are engineers.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some doctors are teachers.

II. Some engineers are teachers.

III. Some doctors are scientists.

options.text: Only conclusions II and III follow
Only conclusions I and III follow
Only conclusions I and II follow

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statement is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/55b56ac7a6276bc52bcb81619c4c76bae09c5a743a6545d927f0f04422065417.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some doctors are teachers → Follow (As, some teachers are scientists and all scientists are doctors. So, as whole scientists comes in doctors and have some part common with teachers therefore it is definitely true.)

II. Some engineers are teachers → Follow (As, some teachers are scientists, all scientists are doctors and all doctors are engineers. So, as whole scientists comes in doctors which whole comes in engineers and some part of scientists is common with teachers therefore it is definitely true.)

III. Some doctors are scientists → Follow (As, all scientists are doctors. So, as whole scientists comes in doctors therefore it is definitely true.)

So, All conclusions follow.

Hence, the correct answer is "**All conclusions follow**".

questions.question:
Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

Some colours are rainbows.

Some paints are rainbows.

All rainbows are drawings.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some drawings are colours.

II. All paints are drawings.

III. Some drawings are rainbows.

options.text: Only conclusions I and II follow
Only conclusions I and III follow
Only conclusions II and III follow

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statement is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c841913056520fe616e4881a50460dffc51a6982e34edf92dd882a92f3634c74.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some drawings are colours → Follow (As, some colours are rainbows and all rainbows are drawings. So, as whole rainbows comes in drawings and have some part common with colours therefore it is definitely true.)

II. All paints are drawings → Does not Follow (As, some paints are rainbows and all rainbows are drawings. So, it is possible but not definitely true)

III. Some drawings are rainbows → Follow (As, all rainbows are drawings. So, as whole rainbows comes in drawings and have some part common with colours therefore it is definitely true.)

So, Only conclusions I and Ill follow.

Hence, the correct answer is "Only conclusions I and Ill follow".

Given : C _ R C _ R _ A R _ A _ C A _ 

By checking options :

 
• R A C A C A → C **__R__** R C __A__ R __C__ A R **__A__** A **__C__** C A **__A__** → (It doesn't Follows the pattern)
 
• R A C A A C → C **__R__** R C __A__ R __C__ A R **__A__** A __R__ C A **__C__** → (It doesn't Follows the pattern)
 
• A C R A C R → C __A__ R C **__C__** R **__R__** A R **__A__** A **__C__** C A __R__ → (It doesn't Follows the pattern)
 
• A A C C R R → C __**A**__ R C __**A**__ R __**C**__ A R __**C**__ A __**R**__ C A __**R**__ → (It follows the pattern of : CAR - CAR - CAR - CAR - CAR)

questions.question:
Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series?

3, 8, 15, 26, 39, ?
questions.solution:
**Logic :** Addition of consecutive prime number is followed here.

**So, the series here is :-**

3 + 5 = 8

8 + 7 = 15

15 + 11 = 26

26 + 13 = 39

39 + 17 = **56**

Hence, **"56"** is the correct answer.
